text:
Asha: noticed a spike in ingest cardinality after last week's SDK update; central enrichment exploded tags for several services. thinking proxy-side lightweight enrichment might reduce central index churn.
Ravi: can you show the before/after span envelope? even a tiny example helps.
Asha: pasted minimal span we see at edge: ```
{
  "trace_id": "t987",
  "spans": [{ "id": "s1", "svc": "payments", "attrs": { "region": "us-west-2", "plan": "starter" } }]
}
```
Asha: central enricher expands `plan` into multiple cohort tags and tenant buckets which increases storage cardinality and query fanout.
Jo: if proxy enriches, we avoid doing the same joins repeatedly in central. downside: extra bytes on every request and more CPU on proxies.
Marta: we should be selective: only move deterministic, low-cardinality attrs (service, env, release, region). Keep high-cardinality user attrs centralized and only on sampled traces.
Owen: important: we need a reliable handshake so central doesn't re-enrich. propose header `X-Proxy-Enriched: v1` + signed blob `X-Enrich-Signature` to prevent spoofing.
Ravi: signature has to be verifiable and support rotation. security-bot: suggest HMAC-SHA256 of the enriched attributes with a key per-proxy-group; put key id in header `X-Enrich-KeyId`. Rotate keys quarterly and support grace period.
Jo: agree. enricher must verify signature and if valid, skip enrichment for fields covered by the signature. also log a metric when signature verification fails: `enrich.signature.fail`.
Marta: rollout: 1) implement allowlist `proxy_enrich.allowlist` in config (per-service/namespace) 2) proxy emits `X-Proxy-Enriched: v1` and `X-Enrich-KeyId`+`X-Enrich-Signature` when enabled 3) central enricher verifies and becomes idempotent 4) canary 1% -> monitor ingest-cardinality, query latency, and `enrich.signature.fail` -> increase.
Asha: egress math: for payments median add is ~95 bytes/span. at 15k qps that's ~1.4MB/s or ~3.6TB/month, ~ $2.4k/mo region. But central index growth is harder to cost-model; short-term we can accept egress if it stabilizes cardinality long-term.
Ravi: let's instrument these new metrics: `proxy.enrich.bytes`, `proxy.enrich.count`, `enricher.skips` and attach to per-service dashboards. ci-bot: will auto-create a grafana panel template when RFC merges.
Owen: edge-case: mixed fleet where some proxies enrich and others don't. central must handle absent header gracefully and only rely on signature when present. also plan for retries where frontends resend spans; signature should include a deterministic path to avoid mismatch.
Marta: tests: unit tests for signature verification and idempotency, e2e with mixed proxies, perf bench for proxy CPU at 95th percentile, and billing dashboard regression test.
Asha: security step: Ravi, coordinate with security to get key management flow; Owen: add header spec and canonicalization rules (order of attrs, whitespace). Jo: draft the allowlist and default deny semantics. Marta: write canary runbook + success criteria (ingest-cardinality down by >20% without >1% query error regression).
Ravi: will also add an opt-out console toggle per-service `enrichment.proxy.enabled=false`. prefer gradual opt-in to be safe.
security-bot: note recorded: key rotation policy created; please add KMS integration in RFC.
Asha: thanks all. I'll assemble a short RFC with header formats, allowlist schema, metrics, and rollout timeline. aim to post for review today. :rocket:
ci-bot: quick check: unit test scaffolding added to the repo PR once RFC lands.
